subject.title: Feature: temp artifact provenance + durable-path guardrails to prevent /tmp chaos

question: Should OpenClaw core own a general temp-artifact provenance and cleanup model, or only runtime-critical temp-path guardrails plus a minimal plugin/skill seam?
rationale: The remaining work affects core storage ownership, cleanup authority, agent/tool APIs, and the boundary between safety defaults and workflow-specific janitor behavior, which requires maintainer product intent before implementation.

options.title: Core Guardrails Plus Minimal Provenance Seam
options.body: Core would cover runtime-critical temp-path checks and a SQLite-backed provenance contract for OpenClaw-owned artifacts, while workflow-specific classes live in plugins or ClawHub packages.

options.title: Full Core Provenance Registry
options.body: Core would own artifact classification, durable routing, and cleanup semantics for all first-class OpenClaw temp artifacts, accepting broader state and janitor responsibility.

options.title: Plugin Or Skill Workflow Only
options.body: Core would stay unchanged except for concrete bug reports, and the audit/janitor classification workflow would be published through ClawHub.

recommendation.title: Core Guardrails Plus Minimal Provenance Seam
recommendation.body: Core would cover runtime-critical temp-path checks and a SQLite-backed provenance contract for OpenClaw-owned artifacts, while workflow-specific classes live in plugins or ClawHub packages.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest available history across temp guardrails and core/plugin scope decisions for this item.
